messages:
Sam W: getting multiple support pings about /v1/generate latency from us-west clients — p99 jumped ~4-5x starting ~23:11 UTC. Anyone oncall? @Maria V? :eyes:
Maria V: on it. I see a correlating spike in TLS handshake times in the edge metrics dashboard. CPU on edge nodes looks normal. Plot: p50 ~50ms, p99 ~1.1s.
Sam W: logs show retries at the TCP/TLS layer, connection gets established but there are 2-3 extra RTTs. Looks like a routing hairpin for some clients.
Ajay Patel: grabbing traceroutes from our closest pops to a few client IPs. sample mtr from pop-us-west-2a to client ip: 
```
Start: pop-us-west-2a
 1. 10.4.0.1
 2. 198.51.100.5
 3. 203.0.113.22 (isp-exit)
 4. 52.23.140.11 (aws-us-west-2b)
 5. 3.80.12.45 (aws-us-east-1a)
```
That hop to us-east-1a looks wrong — traffic is crossing regions then back.
Tim C: checking BGP and route controller logs. I see a withdraw and reannounce for the anycast prefix from our transit peer at 23:10:58 UTC. Looks like a transient path change at the ISP level.
Maria V: DIG +trace from multiple resolvers shows inconsistent A record selection across client ISPs — some resolve to pop-us-west-2a, others to pop-us-east-1a. TTL on our DNS for that record is 30s (we recently lowered it).
Sam W: so two compounding things: short DNS TTL + ISP path flip = some clients rapidly re-resolve and pick a far pop -> extra latency and extra TLS handshakes.
Ajay Patel: quick mitigation idea: reweight anycast to steer traffic away from the flaky peer and bump DNS TTL temporarily to reduce churn. I'll coordinate the reweight.
Sam W: do it. Also create an incident ticket and let support know to reply with the standard latency template.
route-controller-bot: route-controller: applying reweight -20% to pop-us-west-2a for prefix 203.0.113.0/24 (initiated by Ajay) at 23:20:12 UTC :gear:
Ajay Patel: reweight applied. Starting canary: 10% of affected prefix now steered to alternative path. Monitoring p99 in 2m.
support-bot: support: incident INC-2026-078 created for customer-reported latency. Notified customers who reported.
Tim C: bumped DNS TTL for edge-anycast A records from 30 -> 300 seconds to reduce rapid rebalances. Note: some resolver caches might still poll for old answers for a short period.
Maria V: after reweight + TTL bump p99 reduced from ~1.1s -> ~260ms in the next 5m. No errors increased.
Sam W: nice. Can we make this durable? Long-term fixes: 1) work with transit to avoid flappy paths for our prefix, 2) revert to longer DNS TTL by default (>=300s) unless we need ephemeral testing, 3) add BGP flap dampening/monitoring on route-controller, 4) update runbook for anycast route-flap + DNS interplay.
Ajay Patel: will open task items and a PR for runbook updates. Also recommend adding a fallback route policy that keeps traffic local to the region when possible.
Tim C: filed RFC to update default TTL and add a route-controller alert for >X withdraws in Y minutes.
Sam W: support: send customers an update: root cause (transit path churn -> cross-region hairpin + low DNS TTL), mitigation steps taken, and ETA for full remediation. Use template in #support-templates. :white_check_mark:
Maria V: recording timeline for postmortem: 23:10:58 UTC — transit withdraw; 23:11:30 — p99 begins to rise; 23:20:12 — reweight applied; 23:23:00 — DNS TTL bumped; 23:26:30 — p99 back near normal.
Sam W: good job. Action items assigned: Ajay - route-controller runbook PR; Tim - RFC + alerting; Maria - postmortem draft; Support - customer comms. We'll follow up in the incident channel. :memo:
